title: Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, Public Law 101-336 (especially Title II, Section 223)
description: The foundational statute that established paratransit as a civil right. Title II, Section 223 is the operative provision for transit requiring entities operating fixed-route bus service to provide paratransit service that is comparable to fixed-route service, in a service area defined as three-quarter-mile corridor on each side of the fixed route. This is the hard-won result of activist groups such as the Gang of 19 advocating for their rights.
subject: Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990;  Paratransit; Transportation Policy; Civil Rights
rights: Public domain, work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. § 105)

filename: Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Implementing Regulations (45 CFR Part 84).pdf
title: Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Implementing Regulations (45 CFR Part 84)
description: Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. This is a legal precursor to the ADA's transit provisions. It prohibited disability discrimination by any program receiving federal financial assistance covering virtually every public transit agency in the country. The implementing regulations published in May, 1977 followed the legendary 504 sit-in at the San Francisco federal building (April 5th to May 1st, 1977).
subject: Disability rights; Paratransit; Transportation Policy
rights: Public domain, work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. § 105)

title: FTA C 4710.1 - Guidance on ADA Paratransit Service
description: This is the Department of Transportation's operational guidance to transit agencies on ADA paratransit compliance. It translates the statue and the regulation into specific instructions on eligibility, service area, response time, fares, capcity constraints, and conditions under which a public transit agency may contract paratransit service out to a private contractor like JustGo!. This is the federal document that authorizes the privatization of paratransit services. In addition, it defines capacity constraint, a loophole used to justify service cuts and disinvestment in the post-ADA era.
subject: Federal Transit Administration; Paratransit; Americans with Disabilities Act; Public-private partnerships
rights: Public domain, work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. § 105)

title: Disability section of handbook published by the California DMV
description: State driver handbook published by the California Department of Motor Vehicles. This includes sections on disability parking placards (issuance, eligibility, renewal, display rules) of drivers of disabled persons. It also includes details about accessible parking enforcement (fines) and many examples of disability placard abuse. This is the regulatory context in which an individual becomes eligible for paratransit service.
